action.construct-factory.label: Construct — Factory
action.construct-factory.rule: Each of the Chronobot’s Construct Actions is for a specific building type (or Superproject). When using the Construct Action, the Chronobot always picks the building with the higher VP value. If tied, it takes the one in the secondary stack. If it already has 3 buildings of the desired type, it takes nothing (but it still places an Exosuit to block a Construct Action space, and takes 1 VP, as usual, for Failed Actions).

action.construct-superproject.label: Construct — Superproject
action.construct-superproject.rule:
Each of the Chronobot’s Construct Actions is for a specific building type (or Superproject). When using the Construct Action, the Chronobot always picks the building with the higher VP value. If tied, it takes the one in the secondary stack. If it already has 3 buildings of the desired type, it takes nothing (but it still places an Exosuit to block a Construct Action space, and takes 1 VP, as usual, for Failed Actions).

When Constructing a Superproject, the Chronobot first discards a Breakthrough (of any shape or icon; if it has multiples, it discards one of whichever it has the most of—choose one randomly if tied). Then, it takes the highest-VP, face-up Superproject from the Present or any past Era (oldest if tied).

If “Construct Superproject” is rolled and the Chronobot does not have a Breakthrough to discard or it already has 3 Superprojects, it does nothing (but it still places an Exosuit to block a Construct Action space and takes the 1 VP as usual for Failed Actions).

action.evacuation.label: Evacuation
action.evacuation.rule: The Chronobot never takes the Evacuation Action.
action.mine-resource.label: Mine Resource
action.mine-resource.rule:
When taking the Mine Resource Action, the Chronobot determines which 2 Resources it wants the most.

• It prioritizes Resources it does not have.
• If tied, it chooses based on the following priority:

Neutronium > Uranium > Gold > Titanium

Then, it takes the Mine Resource Action space from which these 2 Resources can be gained. If multiple possibilities are available, it selects the topmost one.

Once it has at least one of all 4 Resource types, it discards one of each and gains 5 VPs.
action.reboot.label: Reboot
action.reboot.rule: Each time “Reboot” is selected, the Chronobot simply does nothing. This does not count as a Failed Action, and it does not receive 1 VP.
action.recruit-genius-research.label: Recruit Genius / Research
action.recruit-genius-research.rule: When using the Recruit Genius/Research Action, perform a Recruit Action (see previous page) only if a Genius is available, taking it along with 1 VP (even the Chronobot already has a Genius). If no Genius is available, perform a Research Action instead (see above).
action.recruit.label: Recruit
action.recruit.rule:
When taking the Recruit Action, the Chronobot takes a Worker type it does not yet have, following the priority order below. If this Worker type is unavailable, it takes an available type, following the priority order. It does not receive its respective Recruit bonus; however, it receives 1 VP regardless of the Worker type.

Genius > Administrator > Engineer > Scientist

Once it has at least one of all 4 Worker types, it discards one of each and gains 5 VPs.
action.remove-anomaly.label: Remove Anomaly
action.remove-anomaly.rule:
Each time “Remove Anomaly” is selected, it discards any 2 Resource cubes. Choose Resources it has the most of; if tied, the order of priority is:

Titanium > Gold > Uranium > Neutronium

1 Neutronium cube is equal to 2 non-Neutronium cubes when calculating priority and discarding. Then, if it has the Resources to discard, it removes 1 Anomaly. If it doesn’t have an Anomaly or the Resources to remove one, it takes 1 VP instead as usual for Failed Actions.
action.research.label: Research
action.research.rule: When using the Research Action, only roll the shape die, taking any Breakthrough of the rolled shape.
action.time-travel.label: Time Travel
action.time-travel.rule:
When “Time Travel” is selected, it removes any one Warp tile from the past Timeline tile where the Chronobot has the most Warp tiles (oldest if tied). If a Warp tile was removed the Chronobot advances one step on the Time Travel track.

The Chronobot does not place any Exosuits on a Time Travel Action. If there are no Warp tiles left on the Timeline, the Action is failed, and it scores 1 VP as usual.

instr.doomsday.prepare.done: Place one of the Chronossus’s Path markers on a face-up Experiment that does not already have one — a Level 1 before a Level 2, and the furthest in the past on the Timeline to break a tie.

instr.doomsday.track.up.vp: Move the {tracker} marker one step up the Doomsday track. The Chronossus scores the {vp} VP printed there.

instr.pioneers.adventure.neither: It does not meet either drawn card’s Power requirement — the Chronossus gains 1 VP and both cards go to the bottom of their decks.
instr.pioneers.adventure.noSlot.detail: No free Power slot was left on the Adventure board, so it takes -3 instead.
instr.pioneers.adventure.power: Power {power} before the roll — {base} on its Upgrade board, {slot} from the Path marker — so it draws 2 cards from the {deck} deck. The Adventure die adds {die}, for a total Power of {total}.

instr.pioneers.card.timeTravel.other: advances {n} steps on the Time Travel track

instr.pioneers.upgrade.vpToken: Power Upgrade: the Chronossus has no Resource with a free slot, so it places 1 VP token from the supply on its Exosuit Upgrade board instead.
instr.pioneers.upgrade.vpToken.detail: These VP tokens add Power but do NOT count as VP for the Chronossus, unless that difficulty option is on.
phase.actions.name: Action Rounds
phase.actions.overview: Action rounds phase – Players alternate taking Actions on their Player boards and the Main board until everyone has passed.
phase.actions.rules: On the Chronobot’s turn, roll the AI die. ① The Chronobot performs the Action shown above or below the token with that number, ② then advances the token to the next position. ③ If there are already two tokens there, move the top one to the next position prior to moving the active token.
phase.chronossus.actions.name: Action Rounds
phase.chronossus.actions.overview: Action rounds phase – Players alternate taking Actions until everyone has passed.
phase.chronossus.actions.rules: On the Chronossus’s turn, roll the AI die. It performs the Action shown above or below (possibly on an Action tile) the token with that number, then the token advances. If a token lands on an Autoleap symbol, that tile’s Action resolves immediately and the token advances one more.
phase.chronossus.cleanup.name: Clean Up
phase.chronossus.cleanup.overview: Clean up phase – Retrieve Workers and Exosuits, check for Impact and game end, and set the players’ Focus marker on the next Era.
phase.chronossus.cleanup.rules: Just like with the Chronobot, retrieve the Chronossus’s Exosuits along with your own. After the Impact, flip Collapsing Capital tiles normally.
phase.chronossus.era0warp.name: Era Zero Warp
phase.chronossus.era0warp.overview: Era Zero – Before the regular round sequence for Era 1, a single Warp phase is played, placing Warp tiles on the Era Zero tile. No other phases happen first.
phase.chronossus.era0warp.rules: At the beginning of the game, before starting the regular round sequence for Era 1, perform a Warp Phase (but no other Phases), placing the Warp tiles on the Era Zero tile. Then, proceed with Era 1 as usual, including performing a Preparation Phase and a Paradox Phase (which would usually be skipped in the first Era). You may not warp an Exosuit during the Era Zero Warp Phase.
phase.chronossus.paradox.name: Paradox
phase.chronossus.paradox.overview: Paradox phase – Players who strained the Timeline with Warping roll for Paradoxes. Skipped in the first Era.
phase.chronossus.paradox.rules: The Chronossus rolls for Paradoxes last. If the Chronossus gains an Anomaly, it stops rolling (like you would), then removes any one Warp tile from the Timeline tile where it has the most Warp tiles (oldest if tied). If it would gain an Anomaly when it already has 3 Anomalies, it does not receive another one, nor does it remove a Warp tile.
phase.chronossus.powerup.name: Power Up
phase.chronossus.powerup.overview: Power up phase – Players may power up Exosuits, allowing their Workers to perform Actions on the Main board.
phase.chronossus.powerup.rules: When it is the Chronossus’s turn to decide, draw 3 tokens from its Energy Pool. Before the Impact it powers up 3+X Exosuits (max 6); after the Impact, 2+X (max 4), where X = the non-exhausted Energy Cores drawn. Then return 1 drawn Exhausted Energy Core to the Pool and remove the other drawn tokens from the game.
phase.chronossus.preparation.name: Preparation
phase.chronossus.preparation.overview: Preparation phase – Reveal the Superproject above the next Timeline tile, shift the building stacks, fill up the supply of Workers and Resources available for this Era.
phase.chronossus.warp.name: Warp
phase.chronossus.warp.overview: Warp phase – Players may place Warp tiles on the current Timeline tile to bring assets from the future to the present.
phase.chronossus.warp.rules: Warping occurs in player order. For the Chronossus’s Warp, roll the Paradox die. Place Warp tiles for the Chronossus equal to the rolled number of Paradoxes. The Chronossus does not gain anything for its Warp tiles, and it does not matter which warp tile it places. You choose 0-2 Warp tiles to place as normal.
phase.cleanup.name: Clean Up
phase.cleanup.overview: Clean up phase – Retrieve Workers and Exosuits from the Action spaces, check for Impact and game end, and set the players’ Focus marker on the next Era.
phase.cleanup.rules: Retrieve the Chronobot’s Exosuits along with your own, as normal. After the Impact, follow the usual procedure for flipping Collapsing Capital tiles.
phase.paradox.name: Paradox
phase.paradox.overview: Paradox phase – Players who excessively strained the Timeline with Warping have to roll for Paradoxes. This phase is skipped in the first Era.
phase.paradox.rules: The Chronobot rolls for Paradoxes last. If the Chronobot gains an Anomaly, it stops rolling (like you would), then removes any one Warp tile from the Timeline tile where it has the most Warp tiles (oldest if tied). If it would gain an Anomaly when it already has 3 Anomalies, it does not receive another one, nor does it remove a Warp tile.
phase.powerup.name: Power Up
phase.powerup.overview: Power up phase – Players may power up Exosuits, allowing their Workers to perform Actions on the Main board.
phase.powerup.rules: In pre-Impact Eras, the Chronobot always powers up 6 Exosuits, while in post-Impact Eras, it powers up 4. The Chronobot neither gains nor spends Energy Cores or Water. Powered-up Exosuit markers are piled on top of each other on the upper right Hex-shaped slot.

phase.warp.name: Warp
phase.warp.overview: Warp phase – Players may place Warp tiles on the current Timeline tile to bring assets from the future to the present.

rule.blink:
Whenever the Chronossus is about to take an Action with an Exosuit, perform the following check:
Does it have a Blink-ready Exosuit and at least 1 token in the Flux Pool?
• If not, proceed to Exosuit placement as normal.
• If yes, draw 1 token from the Flux Pool to perform a Blink check.
» If it is a Flux Core, discard it, then perform a Blink (see below).
» If it is an Empty Flux Casing, put it aside. The Chronossus places an Exosuit or passes, as usual.

BLINKING
You Blink following the standard rules, as explained in the Fractures of Time expansion. When the Chronossus decides to Blink (see the check above), it must first select which Exosuit to Blink with (if there are multiple Blink-ready ones):
• (A) If any Exosuits are on an Action corresponding to any Command tokens (other than the one currently selected) on the Chronossus’s board, select that Exosuit. If multiple Exosuits meet this requirement, pick the one that matches the Command token with the smaller number.
• (B) If no Exosuits match a Command token, choose the bottom-left-most one (closest to the bottom Research space). Priority goes to Exosuits on lower spaces, if two are tied.
rule.chronobotSetup.bullets:
• The Chronobot receives its 6 Exosuits and 8 Warp tiles; it does not receive any Starting Assets or Workers.
• Leave all Endgame Condition cards in the box.
• Place the Chronobot board next to the Main board, and place the 4 Command tokens on the 4 marked positions. The Chronobot does not use a Focus marker.
• Place the Chronobot’s Banner on the First Player spot; it is the First Player in the 1st Era. You receive 1 additional Water (for being the second player).
• You may still choose to use either the “A” or the “B” side of your Player board.
• For a more challenging game, use the variant rule described in the base game rulebook: cover the right World Council space with a Hex Unavailable tile.
rule.chronobotSetup.intro: Set up a 2-player game, with the Chronobot as one of the players. Use the Chronobot side of the Solo board. In addition to using the Chronobot’s side of the Solo board, the following changes need to be made during setup:
rule.chronossusEndgame: In addition to your points collected during the game, you score points for the highest level you reached on each Solo Objective. The Chronossus does not lose VPs for its Warp tiles remaining on the Timeline. It scores 1 VP per Breakthrough, plus 2 additional VPs for each complete shape set. If you have more points than the Chronossus, you win; otherwise, you lose.
rule.chronossusPassing:
Once the Chronossus has run out of Exosuits, it will pass the next time it needs to execute an Action that would require placing an Exosuit. Its Command token does not advance when it passes. Actions that place no Exosuit (such as Time Travel or Reboot) never trigger a pass.

Once both you and the Chronossus have passed, the Action Rounds Phase ends. Unlike the Chronobot, the Chronossus has no minimum number of Actions it must take.
rule.cx.altTimelines.difficulty: **INCREASING THE DIFFICULTY:** The Chronossus scores 3 VPs per positive effect.
rule.cx.altTimelines.scoring: It ignores penalties (red spaces), and it receives 2 VPs instead of any positive rewards. You resolve both positive and negative effects as normal.
rule.cx.altTimelines.warp: **WARP PHASE:** In the Warp Phase, you must decide how many Resources and/or Workers to warp first, then roll for the Chronossus. Place the tiles in turn order, as usual.
rule.cx.quantumLoops.action: **ACTION ROUNDS PHASE:** The Chronossus does not actually interact with Quantum Loops. It never “returns” them, thus cards removed during the Warp Phase are permanently removed. When you return a card, add it back to the row of Quantum Loop cards farthest from the draw deck.
rule.cx.quantumLoops.removeOn5: **INCREASING THE DIFFICULTY:** Also remove a Quantum Loop card on a roll of 5.
rule.cx.quantumLoops.twoVp: **INCREASING THE DIFFICULTY:** When removing a Quantum Loop card, the Chronossus receives 2 VPs.
rule.cx.quantumLoops.warp: **WARP PHASE:** In each Warp Phase, when the Chronossus places at least one warp tile, roll the AI die. On a roll of 4, remove the Quantum Loop card farthest from the draw deck from play.
rule.cx.targetedHypersync: Instead of randomly selecting a Hypersync Action space to take, the Chronossus takes the one corresponding to one of your pending Hypersync tiles. If you have more than one, it takes the one furthest in the past.
rule.cx.variableAnomalies.receiving: **RECEIVING ANOMALIES:** When receiving Anomalies, the Chronossus will select one that will allow it to retrieve a Warp tile. If both or neither do, it will select the one with the smaller VP penalty.
rule.cx.variableAnomalies.setup: **CHANGES AT SETUP:** The Chronossus ignores all unique effects of the Anomalies and does not receive an Anomaly Remover tile.
rule.cxSetup.base:
Set up a 2-player game with the Chronossus as one of the players. In addition to using the Chronossus’s side of the Solo board, the following changes need to be made during set-up:

• The Chronossus receives its 6 Exosuits and 8 Warp tiles. It does not receive any Starting Assets or Workers.
• Leave all Endgame Condition cards in the box and shuffle all Solo Objective cards, revealing 3. Return the rest to the box.
• Place the Chronossus board next to the Main board, and place the 4 Command tokens on the 4 marked positions. The Chronossus does not use a Focus marker.
• Place the Action tiles (marked side up) on the empty spaces of the Chronossus board: C01A, C02A, C03A. (Suggested for your first game; later you may assign them randomly.)
• Fill the Chronossus’s Energy Pool container with 5 Energy Core tokens and 5 Exhausted Energy Core tokens.
• Place the Chronossus’s Banner on the First Player spot; it is the First Player in the 1st Era. You receive 1 additional Water (for being the second player).
• You may still choose to use either the “A” or the “B” side of your Player board.
• For a more challenging game, cover the right World Council space with a Hex Unavailable tile.
rule.cxSetup.doomsday:
This requires the Classic Expansion Pack to play. All of the Doomsday module and the Chronossus base rules apply, unless noted below. We suggest using the “Planned Experiments” variant the first few times you play this against the Chronossus.

Place the following Action tiles (with the marked sides face up) on the empty spaces of the Chronossus board: C07A to the (I) empty space, C08A to the (II) empty space. Leave C03A in play.

Add the “Completed Experiments” Solo Objective card to the Solo Objective deck.
rule.cxSetup.doomsdayTracker: If it successfully took an Experiment and the Doomsday tracks aren’t yet locked, it moves its preferred marker (Seal Fate or Save Earth), taking any printed VP on it—regardless of which Path that VP belongs to. The Chronossus’s preferred marker is always the opposing one to yours. For example, if you are playing as the Path of Harmony, thus interacting with the Save Earth marker, it will move the Seal Fate marker on its turn as if it was the Path of Salvation.
rule.cxSetup.fractures:
Setup the Valley board as if it was a 2-Player game.

Place the following Action tiles (with the marked sides face up) on the empty spaces of the Chronossus board: C04A, C05A and C06A.

You will need a second container, referred to as the “Flux Pool.” At setup, add 1 Flux Core and all 3 Empty Flux Casing tokens to it.

The Chronossus does not use a Fracture Device.

Add the “Technology Cards” and “Flux on Track” Solo Objective cards to the deck before drawing.
rule.cxSetup.guardians:

Add the “Successful Adventures” Solo Objective card to the Solo Objective deck.

Give it the Chronossus Exosuit Upgrade board with the “A” side up.
rule.cxSetup.quantumLoops:
This requires the Future Imperfect expansion to play. All of the Quantum Loops module and Chronossus base rules apply, unless noted below.

No changes at Setup. Keep the Quantum Loop cards in a row, adding new ones closest to the draw deck.
rule.doomsday.checkForImpact:
CLEAN UP PHASE — CHANGES
B) CHECK FOR IMPACT
At the beginning of the Check for Impact phase of each Era, roll the two Trajectory dice, then count the total number of (-) and (+) symbols
• on the Trajectory die roll’s result;
• next to the Doomsday track slots where the “Save Earth” and “Seal Fate” Trackers currently are.
Three things can happen based on the result:
1. If there are more (+) symbols in total than (-), move the Impact tile 1 space to the right on the Timeline track if possible — the Impact will occur one Era later.
2. If there are more (-) symbols in total than (+), move the Impact tile 1 space to the left on the Timeline track — the Impact will occur one Era earlier. If this would move the Impact tile behind the current Era tile, do not move the Impact tile.
3. If the number of (-) and (+) symbols is equal, do not move the Impact tile.

IMPORTANT: If the “Seal Fate” tracker is on the bottommost spot of the Doomsday track during the Check for Impact phase, do not roll the Trajectory dice - instead, place the Impact tile after the current Timeline tile (regardless of its position) and resolve the Impact immediately.

IMPORTANT: If the “Save Earth” tracker is on the topmost spot of the Doomsday track, the Impact’s damage to the present is completely mitigated, and the game is over — proceed to Ending the Game. In games where Earth is saved, the Impact is never resolved, so there will be no Evacuation - try to adjust your game plan accordingly!
rule.endgame: The Chronobot does not lose VPs for its Warp tiles that remain on the Timeline. It scores 1 VP per Breakthrough, plus 2 additional VPs for each complete shape set. If you have more points than the Chronobot, you win; otherwise, you lose.
rule.hypersyncParadox:
During the Paradox Phase, the presence of a Hypersync tile counts as a Warp tile when checking for most Warp tiles per Timeline tile. Therefore, if a player has two Warp tiles on a Timeline tile, while another has a single Warp tile and a Hypersync tile, they both roll for Paradox.

IMPORTANT: Just like in the base game, players that have zero Warp tiles on a Timeline tile do not roll for a Paradox, even if they have a Hypersync tile present.

Additionally, the player (or players) with the most total Hypersync tiles (across all Timeline tiles) in play make one more Paradox roll, unless they have already received an Anomaly during the current Paradox Phase. (If no player has any Hypersync tiles in play, this roll is skipped.)
rule.mechPlacement.0: The Chronobot does not use Workers to take Main board Actions, only empty Exosuits.
rule.mechPlacement.1: It ignores everything printed on Action spaces or Collapsing Capital tiles and never pays the costs of Actions. It cannot place on face-down Collapsing Capital tiles.
rule.mechPlacement.2: It always picks the topmost available space on Capital Actions.
rule.mechPlacement.3: If there are no available spaces on a Capital Action the Chronobot rolled, it places on a World Council Action space instead, always taking the First Player spot if possible.
rule.passing:
Once the Chronobot has run out of Exosuits, it takes a Time Travel Action on its next turn (if able), then passes. However, if you pass first, and the Chronobot has taken at least 3 Actions, the Action Rounds Phase ends immediately. If the Chronobot has not yet taken 3 Actions, it will continue taking turns until it has, at which point the Action Rounds Phase would end.

NOTE: You can use an unused Path’s Exosuits to track the number of Actions the Chronobot takes, especially if you decide to raise the number of Actions to 6.

NOTE: The Chronobot will never take fewer than 3 Actions.
rule.playerScoring: Tally up points from buildings, Anomalies, Superprojects, Time Travel, Morale, Victory Point tokens, Timeline penalties and Endgame Conditions using the scoring pad provided. Each individual Breakthrough is worth 1 VP. In addition, a set of three Breakthroughs with different shapes (i.e. Circle, Triangle, Square; the icons do NOT have to match) is worth an additional 2 VP/set.

tile.C04A.detail:
NEW ACTION: ASSIMILATE
Before the Chronossus performs the Assimilate Action, roll the Research shape die.
On Circle: It recruits an Operator and gains 1 Flux Core.
On Triangle: It takes a Technology card (preferring the secondary stack).
On Square: It either recruits an Operator (and gains 1 Flux Core) or takes a Technology card, whichever it has fewer of (Operator, if tied).
If it attempts to recruit an Operator, and there are none left, it is a Failed Action and takes 1 VP.

RECRUITING OPERATORS
Operators function as wildcards. When taken, place the Operator in the topmost empty space of the Chronossus’s Worker collection. It counts towards that Worker type for all purposes, including discarding for 5 VPs.

GAMEPLAY CHANGES

tile.C07A.detail:
When taking an Experiment Action, the Chronossus places an Exosuit on the Experiment hex pool space and performs two steps, in the following order:

STEP 1: EXECUTE EXPERIMENT
The Chronossus takes an Experiment with a Path marker on it (see Step 2 for adding Path markers) and discards the Path marker. Whether it takes a Level 1 or Level 2 Experiment is shown on the Action tile. If none of that level is available, skip this step. If multiple are available, pick the leftmost available one on the Timeline.

If it successfully took an Experiment and the Doomsday tracks aren’t yet locked, it moves its preferred marker (Seal Fate or Save Earth), taking any printed VP on it—regardless of which Path that VP belongs to. The Chronossus’s preferred marker is always the opposing one to yours. For example, if you are playing as the Path of Harmony, thus interacting with the Save Earth marker, it will move the Seal Fate marker on its turn as if it was the Path of Salvation.

STEP 2: PREPARE FOR EXPERIMENTATION
It places a Path marker on a face-up Experiment card (except the one under the next Era), that does not yet have one on it. (Your Focus marker has no effect on this.) If there are multiple available ones, pick Level 1 before Level 2 ones; if still tied, pick the furthest in the past on the Timeline.

NOTE: It is possible for one of the steps to fail (if none/all of the Experiments have a Path marker, respectively). If this happens, ignore that step.

When you take an Experiment with one of the Chronossus’s Path markers on it, move it onto a face-up Experiment under a later Era (up to the present Era) that does not yet have one. If all of them do, discard the Path marker.
tile.C07A.name: Level 1 Experiment
tile.C07A.rule: The Chronossus executes a Level 1 Experiment then prepares for Experimentation. (See page 14 for details).
tile.C07B.detail:
When taking an Experiment Action, the Chronossus places an Exosuit on the Experiment hex pool space and performs two steps, in the following order:

STEP 1: EXECUTE EXPERIMENT
The Chronossus takes an Experiment with a Path marker on it (see Step 2 for adding Path markers) and discards the Path marker. Whether it takes a Level 1 or Level 2 Experiment is shown on the Action tile. If none of that level is available, skip this step. If multiple are available, pick the leftmost available one on the Timeline.

If it successfully took an Experiment and the Doomsday tracks aren’t yet locked, it moves its preferred marker (Seal Fate or Save Earth), taking any printed VP on it—regardless of which Path that VP belongs to. The Chronossus’s preferred marker is always the opposing one to yours. For example, if you are playing as the Path of Harmony, thus interacting with the Save Earth marker, it will move the Seal Fate marker on its turn as if it was the Path of Salvation.

STEP 2: PREPARE FOR EXPERIMENTATION
It places a Path marker on a face-up Experiment card (except the one under the next Era), that does not yet have one on it. (Your Focus marker has no effect on this.) If there are multiple available ones, pick Level 1 before Level 2 ones; if still tied, pick the furthest in the past on the Timeline.

NOTE: It is possible for one of the steps to fail (if none/all of the Experiments have a Path marker, respectively). If this happens, ignore that step.

When you take an Experiment with one of the Chronossus’s Path markers on it, move it onto a face-up Experiment under a later Era (up to the present Era) that does not yet have one. If all of them do, discard the Path marker.

tile.C09A.detail:
When taking an Adventure Action, it places an Exosuit on the Adventure hex pool space and one of its Path markers on the highest available strength bonus. Then, it performs two steps, in this order:

STEP 1: PERFORM ADVENTURE
Sum up the power on the Chronossus’s Exosuit Upgrade board (including the strength bonus from the Path marker): If 9 or higher, it draws 2 cards from 10+ deck; otherwise, it draws 2 cards from the 5+ deck. Then, it rolls the Adventure die and calculates total power the same way as you would.

It takes the card with the highest power requirement it meets. The unselected card(s) are placed on the bottom of their respective deck(s). If it met neither card’s requirement, it gains 1 VP (and returns both cards to the bottom).
If a card was selected, it receives the card’s benefit then discards the card.

STEP 2: POWER UPGRADE
It takes a Resource from the Chronossus’s board and moves it to its Exosuit Upgrade board.
• It must be a Resource that has an available slot on the board.
• If there are multiple options, it will pick whichever Resource it has the most of.
• If tied, use this order: Titanium > Gold > Uranium > Neutronium.
If it does not have any Resources that can be placed, or there are no slots available, place 1 VP token straight from the supply on the Exosuit upgrade board instead. These VP tokens add further strength to the Chronossus’s power, but they do not count as VP for the Chronossus by default.

NOTE: It is possible for one of these steps to fail. If this happens, ignore that step.

tile.C11A.detail:
NEW ACTION: ACQUIRE GUARDIAN
IF THIS ACTION IS SELECTED BEFORE IMPACT:
• The Chronossus places an Exosuit on the World Council Action space and becomes the First Player (if possible), but it does not perform an Action. Instead, it recruits the leftmost available Guardian at no additional cost.
• If the World Council Action space is already taken, it spends a Worker (Most > Scientist > Engineer > Administrator > Genius), then acquires a Guardian without placing an Exosuit.
If it cannot do either option, or the Impact has already happened, it gains 1 VP, as if it was a Failed Action.

GAMEPLAY CHANGES
When deciding which Exosuit to place, the Chronossus places Guardians last. If it wants to take a Capital Action (Research, Recruit, Construct) and there are no Action spaces remaining (including the World Council Action space), it places a Guardian (if it has any) on the reserved Guardian Action space and performs the Capital Action. This means the Action is not a Failed Action, so it does not take 1 VP.

3 POWER UP PHASE
The Chronossus first powers up as many Guardians as it can, then it powers up its own Exosuits (e.g. if it needs to power up 4 Exosuits and has 2 Guardians, it will power up both of them and 2 of its own).

NEW ACTION: ASSIMILATE
Before the Chronossus performs the Assimilate Action, roll the Research shape die.
On Circle: It recruits an Operator and gains 1 Flux Core.
On Triangle: It takes a Technology card (preferring the secondary stack).
On Square: It either recruits an Operator (and gains 1 Flux Core) or takes a Technology card, whichever it has fewer of (Operator, if tied).
If it attempts to recruit an Operator, and there are none left, it is a Failed Action and takes 1 VP.

Operators function as wildcards. When taken, place the Operator in the topmost empty space of the Chronossus’s Worker collection. It counts towards that Worker type for all purposes, including discarding for 5 VPs.

ui.cx.hs.targetedAsk: Does one of the available Hypersync spaces ({list}) match a **Hypersync tile you have pending** from a **prior Era**?
ui.cx.hs.targetedDefer: It scores 2 VP and retrieves its own oldest pending tile (no Time Travel advance). Don’t place anything yet — the Blink check comes next.
ui.cx.hs.targetedPlace: The Chronossus takes the space matching **your furthest-in-the-past** pending Hypersync tile.
ui.cx.hs.targetedPlaceSub: Place a bot Exosuit on that space to block it; it scores 2 VP and retrieves its own oldest pending tile. (No Time Travel advance.)
ui.cx.hs.timeTravelFallback: Remove one of the Chronossus’s **Warp tiles** from the past Timeline tile where it has the most (oldest if tied), then advance its Time Travel marker.
ui.cx.hs.whyNeither: (no retrievable tile in a prior Era, and no available Exosuit)
ui.cx.hs.whyNoTile: (no retrievable Hypersync tile in a prior Era)
ui.cx.hsTile.instruct: No Action space remained for the “{action}” Action. Place one of the Chronossus’s Solo Hypersync tiles **above Era {era}** and perform the Action normally — no Exosuit is placed, and this is **not** a Failed Action.
ui.cx.hsTile.title: Hypersync tile
ui.cx.impactCheck.earthSaved.detail: Earth is saved: the Impact never happens and the game ends now
ui.cx.impactCheck.earthSaved.label: “Save Earth” reached its topmost slot
ui.cx.impactCheck.impactNow.label: “Seal Fate” reached its bottommost slot
ui.cx.impactCheck.impactOccurred.detail: the Impact tile was reached at the end of this Era
ui.cx.impactCheck.impactOccurred.label: The Impact occurred
ui.cx.pass.alternates: The Chronossus alternates turns with you. It passes once it is out of Exosuits and would place one; when you have both passed, the Action Rounds Phase ends.
ui.cx.pass.outOfFigures: The Chronossus is out of Exosuits — it passes the next time it would place one (Time Travel / Reboot still resolve).
ui.cx.pass.passed: The Chronossus has passed for this Era.
ui.cx.phase.paradoxFractures: Paradox phase – Players who strained the Timeline with Warping roll for Paradoxes. With Fractures of Time it is played in Era 1 as well, since the Era Zero tile is already in the past.
ui.cx.powerUp.powered: Powered up **{n}** Exosuit. Set these aside ready to place on the board for this Era.
ui.cx.powerUp.poweredGuardians: Powered up **{total}** in total — **{guardians}**{exosuits}. It powers up as many Guardians as it can first. Set these aside ready to place on the board for this Era.
ui.cx.powerUp.poweredPlural: Powered up **{n}** Exosuits. Set these aside ready to place on the board for this Era.
ui.cx.powerUp.restRemoved: (the rest are removed from the game)
ui.cx.rules.guardiansGameplay: **GAMEPLAY CHANGES:** When deciding which Exosuit to place, the Chronossus places Guardians last. If it wants to take a Capital Action (Research, Recruit, Construct) and there are no Action spaces remaining (including the World Council Action space), it places a Guardian (if it has any) on the reserved Guardian Action space and performs the Capital Action. This means the Action is not a Failed Action, so it does not take 1 VP.
ui.cx.rules.guardiansPowerUp: **3 POWER UP PHASE:** The Chronossus first powers up as many Guardians as it can, then it powers up its own Exosuits (e.g. if it needs to power up 4 Exosuits and has 2 Guardians, it will power up both of them and 2 of its own).
ui.cx.tile.autoleap: **Autoleap:** the marker moved onto this tile, so its Action activates now — then the Command marker advances one extra space.
ui.cx.upgrade.flagHint: Exosuit Upgrade board ({side} side) — {breakdown}. At {n}+ Power (with the Path-marker bonus) it draws from the 10+ Adventure deck. Tap to open the board.
ui.cx.upgrade.threshold: At **{n}** or more Power — including the Path marker’s bonus, before the die — it draws from the **10+** Adventure deck.
ui.cx.upgrade.title: Exosuit Upgrade board
ui.cx.upgrade.tokenNote: Its {n} VP token adds Power but is **not** VP, unless that difficulty option is on.
ui.cx.upgrade.tokenNotePlural: Its {n} VP tokens add Power but are **not** VP, unless that difficulty option is on.
ui.cx.upgrade.tokensPower: +{n} Power from its VP tokens — tap for the token count
ui.cx.va.ask: **Variable Anomalies — the Chronossus receives an Anomaly.** From the visible Anomaly tiles give it the one that **lets it retrieve a Warp tile** right now (check each tile’s Before/After Impact icon against this Era’s Impact status). If **both or neither** do, give it the one with the **smaller VP penalty** (closer to 0). Tap its printed VP.
ui.cx.va.retrieveAsk: Does the tile it took retrieve a Warp tile?
ui.cx.va.retrieveFrom: If it does: remove one of the Chronossus’s Warp tiles from **{tile}**.
ui.cx.valley.assimilateOperator: The shape die rolled **{shape}** — the Chronossus recruits an **Operator**. Are there any left in the **Valley**?
ui.cx.valley.assimilateTech: The shape die rolled **{shape}** — the Chronossus takes a **Technology card**, preferring the secondary stack.
ui.cx.valley.blinkSub: Don’t place anything yet — the Chronossus Blink-checks first, and a Blink moves an Exosuit it already has on the Main board onto the Valley space instead.
ui.cx.valley.discardOperator: If so, discard one **Operator** from the Valley.
ui.cx.valley.spaceAsk: Is an **{space}** Action space — or the **Valley Capital Action space** — open on the **Valley board**?
ui.cx.valley.spaceAskPlace: Is an **{space}** Action space — or the **Valley Capital Action space** — open on the **Valley board**? Place the Chronossus’s Exosuit on the **topmost** available {space} space, or on the Valley Capital space if no {space} space is open.
ui.cx.valley.techWorth: It is worth 3 VP at the end of the game.
ui.cx.warp.altAsk: Alternate Timelines: how many of the Chronossus’s {n} newly placed Warp tile landed on a **positive**-effect Timeline space?
ui.cx.warp.altAskPlural: Alternate Timelines: how many of the Chronossus’s {n} newly placed Warp tiles landed on a **positive**-effect Timeline space?
ui.cx.warp.altSub: It ignores negative/penalty spaces entirely — nothing to report for those. Each positive one scores it {vp} VP.
ui.cx.warp.altTimelinesIntro: **Alternate Timelines:** decide how many Resources and/or Workers **you** are warping **before** rolling for the Chronossus. Once you've decided, roll below and place the tiles in turn order as usual.
ui.cx.warp.quantumNone: the Chronossus rolled {n} — **no card is removed**. A card only goes on a roll of {faces}.
ui.cx.warp.quantumRemoves: the Chronossus rolled {n} — remove the Quantum Loop card **farthest from the draw deck** from play. It never returns a card, so this one is gone **permanently**.{vp}
ui.cx.warp.quantumVp: It receives {n} VP for the removal.
ui.cxScore.lose: You lose — the Chronossus has at least as many points.
ui.cxScore.numberPlaceholder: Enter your total VP (including Solo Objectives)
ui.cxScore.win: 🎉 You win! (more points than the Chronossus)
ui.cxSetup.adventureDeck.shared.detail: The Chronossus draws from the same decks you do. The app tells you its Power and which deck to draw 2 cards from, and you tell it which cards came up.
ui.cxSetup.adventureDeck.shared.label: Your physical decks
ui.cxSetup.adventureDeck.virtual.detail: The app keeps its own shuffled copy of both Adventure decks, draws for the Chronossus and shows you the card. Your physical decks are never touched, so the bot can’t deplete or reorder them.
ui.cxSetup.adventureDeck.virtual.label: Its own deck (recommended)
ui.cxSetup.app.addObjectives: Add the {cards} Solo Objective card from your module to the deck, then
ui.cxSetup.app.addObjectivesPlural: Add the {cards} Solo Objective cards from your modules to the deck, then
ui.cxSetup.app.banner: Place the Chronossus’s Banner on the First Player spot; it is the First Player in the 1st Era. You receive 1 additional Water (for being the second player).
ui.cxSetup.app.endgameCards: Leave all Endgame Condition cards in the box.
ui.cxSetup.app.figures: The Chronossus receives its 6 Exosuits and 8 Warp tiles. It does not receive any Starting Assets or Workers.
ui.cxSetup.app.guardians.board: Set up the **Guardian board** as for a 2-player game, and keep the Chronossus’s **Path markers** to hand — when it acquires a Guardian you place one on an empty Guardian board slot, and that slot becomes that Guardian’s own Action space. (Solo Path markers aren’t meant to be limited; if they run out, use an unused Path’s markers.)
ui.cxSetup.app.guardians.starting: **Give the Chronossus 1 Guardian now** and place one of its Path markers on an empty Guardian board slot (difficulty option selected).
ui.cxSetup.app.guardians.tracked: The app tracks how many Guardians the Chronossus owns and how many are powered up; you place and retrieve the miniatures as prompted.
ui.cxSetup.app.intro: Set up a 2-player game with the Chronossus as one of the players. There’s no need for the Chronossus board — this app tracks it for you.
ui.cxSetup.app.noFocus: The Chronossus does not use a Focus marker.
ui.cxSetup.app.objectivesNote: In addition to your points collected during the game, you score points for the highest level you reached on each Solo Objective. The bot doesn’t score for Solo Objectives.
ui.cxSetup.app.playerBoard: You may still choose to use either the “A” or the “B” side of your Player board.
ui.cxSetup.app.revealing: {shuffle} all Solo Objective cards, revealing {n}{note}. Return the rest to the box.
ui.cxSetup.app.title: Setup for this app
ui.cxSetup.app.vpNote: This app tracks **all** of the Chronossus’s VP for you and explains each Action’s rules as it takes them. Building VP is counted as tiles are discarded, rather than placed on the bot’s board. Be ready to place Exosuits and Warp tiles to the board and discard pieces for the bot as prompted.
ui.cxSetup.app.worldCouncilOption: **Cover the right World Council space** with a Hex Unavailable tile (difficulty option selected).
ui.cxSetup.app.worldCouncilRequired: **Cover the right World Council space** with a Hex Unavailable tile (required for this mode).
ui.cxSetup.diff.altTimelines3vp.detail: The Chronossus scores 3 VPs per positive effect instead of 2.
ui.cxSetup.diff.altTimelines3vp.label: Alternate Timelines: 3 VP per positive effect
ui.cxSetup.diff.doomsdayNoPlanned.detail: By default the Level 2 Experiment stack sits face up and a claimed Experiment is replaced from it immediately. Without the variant the stack is face down and Level 2 Experiments are dealt under the Timeline in the Preparation phase instead — the rulebook suggests keeping the variant on for your first few games.
ui.cxSetup.diff.doomsdayNoPlanned.label: Doomsday: play without the Planned Experiments variant
ui.cxSetup.diff.doomsdaySeedMarkers.deta: Place 1/2/3 of the Chronossus’s Path markers on future Experiments during setup. They become available to it once they are in the present, so it can execute an Experiment on its very first Experiment Action.
ui.cxSetup.diff.doomsdaySeedMarkers.labe: Doomsday: it starts with Path markers on future Experiments
ui.cxSetup.diff.extraEnergy.detail: Increase the number of Energy Cores by 1/2/3 in the Energy Pool at the beginning of the game.
ui.cxSetup.diff.extraEnergy.label: Extra starting Energy Cores
ui.cxSetup.diff.extraPowerup.detail: The Chronossus powers up one additional Exosuit each Era for free. If this would exceed its maximum number of Exosuits, it gains 2 VPs instead for each excess Energy Core drawn (those Energy Cores are still removed from the game).
ui.cxSetup.diff.extraPowerup.label: One extra powered Exosuit each Era
ui.cxSetup.diff.failedActionVp.detail: The Chronossus gains 2 VPs for each Failed Action.
ui.cxSetup.diff.failedActionVp.label: Failed Actions score VP
ui.cxSetup.diff.fewerObjectives.detail: Play with fewer (or no) Solo Objectives.
ui.cxSetup.diff.fewerObjectives.label: Fewer (or no) Solo Objectives
ui.cxSetup.diff.fracturesC14.detail: C14 is a more difficult tile — Assimilate, but it also gains 1 additional Flux Core.
ui.cxSetup.diff.fracturesC14.label: Fractures: replace C04 with C14
ui.cxSetup.diff.fracturesExtraFlux.detai: Increase the number of Flux Cores in the Flux Pool by 1/2/3 at the beginning of the game — a fuller pool means it Blinks more often.
ui.cxSetup.diff.fracturesExtraFlux.label: Fractures: extra starting Flux Cores
Each leftover Flux Core in the Flux Pool at the end of the game is worth 1 VP to the Chronossus.
ui.cxSetup.diff.fracturesPlayerGlitch.de: Roll the Glitch die after setup and place the rolled Glitch for yourself, in addition to the two starting Glitches from the Fractures of Time rules.
ui.cxSetup.diff.fracturesPlayerGlitch.la: Fractures: roll a starting Glitch for yourself
ui.cxSetup.diff.guardiansPostimpact2vp.d: After the Impact the Chronossus can no longer acquire Guardians. Instead of the usual Failed Action, it scores 2 VPs when it resolves the Acquire Guardian Action.
ui.cxSetup.diff.guardiansPostimpact2vp.l: Guardians: Acquire Guardian scores 2 VP post-Impact
ui.cxSetup.diff.guardiansStart1.detail: The Chronossus starts with 1 Guardian — place one of its Path markers on an empty Guardian board slot at setup, and give it a Guardian.
ui.cxSetup.diff.guardiansStart1.label: Guardians: it starts the game with 1 Guardian
ui.cxSetup.diff.hypersyncTargeted.detail: Instead of randomly selecting a Hypersync Action space to take, the Chronossus takes the one corresponding to one of your pending Hypersync tiles. If you have more than one, it takes the one furthest in the past.
ui.cxSetup.diff.hypersyncTargeted.label: Hypersync: take your oldest tile’s space (no random roll)
ui.cxSetup.diff.leftoverEnergyVp.detail: Each leftover (non-exhausted) Energy Core in the Energy Pool at the end of the game is worth 1 VP to the Chronossus.
ui.cxSetup.diff.leftoverEnergyVp.label: Leftover Energy Cores score VP
ui.cxSetup.diff.pioneersBoardB.detail: The Chronossus starts with a Power value of 3 instead of 2, and each VP token on its Upgrade board is worth 3 Power instead of 2.
ui.cxSetup.diff.pioneersBoardB.label: Pioneers: flip its Exosuit Upgrade board to the B side
ui.cxSetup.diff.pioneersVpTokensCount.de: By default the VP tokens it places when it cannot upgrade a Resource add Power but are not worth VP. With this on, each one also scores 1 VP at the end.
ui.cxSetup.diff.pioneersVpTokensCount.la: Pioneers: VP tokens on the Upgrade board count as VP
ui.cxSetup.diff.ql2vp.detail: When removing a Quantum Loop card, the Chronossus receives 2 VPs.
ui.cxSetup.diff.ql2vp.label: Quantum Loops: 2 VP per card removed
ui.cxSetup.diff.qlRemoveOn5.detail: The Warp Phase check removes a Quantum Loop card on a roll of 4 or 5, not just a 4.
ui.cxSetup.diff.qlRemoveOn5.label: Quantum Loops: also remove a card on a roll of 5
ui.cxSetup.diff.researchNewShape.detail: When taking a Research Action, the Chronossus takes a Breakthrough shape it does not already possess.
ui.cxSetup.diff.researchNewShape.label: Research takes a new Breakthrough shape
ui.cxSetup.diff.swapTiles.detail: Swap the Action tiles between Slot I and Slot III (the two marked spaces).
ui.cxSetup.diff.swapTiles.label: Swap Action tiles between spaces
ui.cxSetup.diff.tilesBSide.detail: Flip some or all of the Action tiles to their B side (pick which below).
ui.cxSetup.diff.tilesBSide.label: Flip Action tiles to their B side
ui.cxSetup.diff.worldCouncil.detail: For a more challenging game, cover the right World Council space with a Hex Unavailable tile. (This constrains your own board — the app changes nothing.)
ui.cxSetup.diff.worldCouncil.label: Cover the right World Council space
ui.cxSetup.difficulty.note: Select one or more options to increase the difficulty against the Chronossus, or play with none for the standard game.
ui.cxSetup.flavor:
When the Path of Unity appeared in our present, altering the course of history, their audacity caused a massive dissonance in the Space-Time Continuum that could not remain unanswered by the cosmos.

From the deepest, darkest recesses of the universe, an ancient and ruthless menace emerged. The Chronossus, the Destroyer of Worlds, has awakened with only one purpose: to eliminate the dissonance and consume all broken timelines, including ours.
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.board: Set up the **Doomsday board**, the Experiment cards and the Impact tile as for a 2-player game — including the {stack}.
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.bothTokens: **You move both physical tokens.** The app tracks where the Chronossus’s marker sits — that is how it knows the VP each of its Experiments earns — and tells you when to advance it. You will need both trackers’ positions yourself each Clean Up, to read the (+) and (−) symbols for the Trajectory roll.
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.checkImpact: **You run Check for Impact yourself** each Clean Up — the app never rolls the Trajectory dice or tracks the Impact tile. It prompts you at the right moment and asks what happened.
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.markers: Keep the Chronossus’s **Path markers** to hand for the Experiments.
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.path: Your Path (**{path}**) puts you on the **{playerTrack}** track — that is the tracker **you** advance for your own Experiments. The Chronossus scores on the **{botTrack}** track, always the opposing one.
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.seedMarkers: Place **{n}** of the Chronossus’s Path markers on future Experiments now (difficulty option selected).
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.stackNoPlanned: face-down Level 2 stack (you chose to play without the Planned Experiments variant)
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.stackPlanned: face-up Level 2 stack of the Planned Experiments variant
ui.cxSetup.mod.doomsday.title: Doomsday setup
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.cores: Keep **cardboard energized cores** to hand — or any alternative marker — to show which of the Chronossus’s Exosuits are ready to Blink: whenever it places an Exosuit on the Main board, put an Energy Core from the supply into that Exosuit.
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.eraZero: Set up the Timeline with the **Era Zero** tile and its own face-up Superproject. Straight after setup the app runs a one-off **Era Zero Warp Phase** — no other phases — with the Warp tiles going on that tile. Era 1 then runs as usual, including its Paradox phase (normally skipped in the first Era).
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.extraFlux: (+{n} extra Flux Core, difficulty option selected)
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.extraFluxPlural: (+{n} extra Flux Cores, difficulty option selected)
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.fluxPool: No need for the physical **Flux Pool** container — the app holds its 1 Flux Core + 3 Empty Flux Casings and draws from it for you{extra}.
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.noDevice: The Chronossus does not use a Fracture Device, never rolls the Flux or Glitch dice, and never receives Glitches.
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.playerGlitch: **Roll the Glitch die and place that Glitch for yourself**, on top of your two starting Glitches (difficulty option selected).
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.timeline: The Timeline is **shorter**: three Eras pre-Impact and two post-Impact. The Impact happens in **Era 3**’s Clean Up and the game ends after **Era 5**.
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.title: Fractures of Time setup
ui.cxSetup.mod.fractures.valley: Set up the **Valley board** as if it was a 2-player game. The app names the Valley Action the Chronossus takes; you place its Exosuit there (or on the Valley Capital space if no Valley Action space is free).
ui.cxSetup.mod.guardians.board: Set up the Guardian board as for a 2-player game, and cover the right World Council Action space with a Hex Unavailable tile (as noted in the Guardians of the Council rules for 2 players).
ui.cxSetup.mod.guardians.markers: Keep the Chronossus’s Path markers to hand for the Guardian board.
ui.cxSetup.mod.guardians.title: Guardians of the Council setup
ui.cxSetup.mod.hypersync.board: Use the 2-player side of the Hypersync board, and cover the right World Council Action space on the Main board with a Hex Unavailable tile (as noted in the Hypersync rules for 2 players).
ui.cxSetup.mod.hypersync.tiles: Place the Solo Hypersync tiles next to the Chronossus board.
ui.cxSetup.mod.hypersync.title: Hypersync Future Actions setup
ui.cxSetup.mod.pioneers.board: Place the Adventure board next to the Main board.
ui.cxSetup.mod.pioneers.markers: Keep the Chronossus’s Path markers to hand for the Adventure board’s Power slots.
ui.cxSetup.mod.pioneers.ownDeck: The app keeps the Chronossus’s **own copy** of both Adventure decks — shuffle your two decks and place them on the Adventure board for yourself only. The bot never draws from them.
ui.cxSetup.mod.pioneers.sharedDeck: Shuffle the 5+ and 10+ Adventure decks onto the Adventure board. The Chronossus draws from these **same decks**, and you tell the app which cards it drew.
ui.cxSetup.mod.pioneers.title: Pioneers of New Earth setup
ui.cxSetup.mod.pioneers.upgrade: Give the Chronossus its Exosuit Upgrade board, **{side}** side up.
ui.cxSetup.mod.quantumLoops.check: The app rolls the check for you each Warp Phase in which the Chronossus places a Warp tile, and tells you whether a card leaves play. It never takes or returns a card itself, so anything it removes is gone **permanently**.
ui.cxSetup.mod.quantumLoops.leak: If you gain the **“Cosmic Data Leak”** card, draw 2 unused Solo Objectives and put them into play.
ui.cxSetup.mod.quantumLoops.module: Set up the **Quantum Loops module** as for a 2-player game — the card offer, the draw deck and the Quantum Warp tiles are unchanged.
ui.cxSetup.mod.quantumLoops.row: Keep the Quantum Loop cards in a **row**, adding new ones **closest to the draw deck**. That order is what the Chronossus reads: it always removes the card **farthest from the draw deck**. When you return a card of your own, add it back farthest from the deck too.
ui.cxSetup.mod.quantumLoops.title: Quantum Loops setup
ui.cxSetup.modules.buildings: The Interlocking buildings and Neutronide buildings are supported and require no additional components or adjustments to the rules.
ui.cxSetup.modules.extras: Optional add-on modules (combine with any base mode above):
ui.cxSetup.modules.note: **Base** is the app designer’s suggested start. The app itself handles the extra bookkeeping and complexity of the other modules, giving you a more complete opponent as they come online across the game modes.
ui.cxSetup.modules.pioneersDeck: **Pioneers — where the Chronossus’s Adventure cards come from.** You can change this later in the ⚙ menu.
ui.cxSetup.path.bothTokens: You will move **both** physical tokens during the game. The app tracks where the Chronossus’s marker sits so it knows the VP its Experiments earn, and tells you when to advance it — and you will read both trackers’ (+)/(−) symbols yourself for the Trajectory roll each Clean Up.
ui.cxSetup.path.detail: You control the **{track}** tracker, moving it {direction} the track. The Chronossus takes the **{botTrack}** tracker.
ui.cxSetup.path.note: Doomsday gives each Path a side of the Doomsday track. Tell the app which one you are playing and it takes the other for the Chronossus — that holds for the whole game.
ui.cxSetup.tileFlip.head: Slot {slot} · {code} — {name}
ui.dialog.anomaly.fail: Failed Action: {reason} — the {bot} takes +{vp} VP instead (no Exosuit placed).
ui.dialog.anomaly.instruct: The {bot} discards **{discards}** and removes **1 Anomaly** from its board.
ui.dialog.anomaly.reason.cubes: it lacks 2 Resource cubes (or a Neutronium) to spend
ui.dialog.anomaly.reason.none: it has no Anomaly to remove
ui.dialog.construct.building: Take the higher-VP **{building}** (secondary stack if tied). Tap its printed VP (1–4) — then discard it.
ui.dialog.construct.superproject: Take the **highest-VP Superproject** (oldest if tied). Tap its printed VP (3–8).
ui.dialog.genius.ask: Is a **Genius** available to recruit **and** an open Recruit Action space (or World Council space)? If so, the {bot} recruits a Genius. If not, it performs a Research action instead.
ui.dialog.genius.recruitPlace: Place the {bot}’s Exosuit on the topmost available **Recruit** Action space (or a World Council space if full) and recruit a **Genius**, removing it from the board. The bot gains 1 VP.
ui.dialog.genius.recruitPlaced: The {bot} recruits a **Genius** from that Recruit space, removing it from the board. The bot gains 1 VP.
ui.dialog.guardian.instruct: No Action space was open, so the {bot} places a **Guardian** on the **Guardian board**, on an open space marked with one of its **Path markers** — and performs the Action from there.
ui.dialog.guardian.sub: It doesn’t matter which of its marked spaces you use. This is **not** a Failed Action, so it takes no +1 VP.
ui.dialog.mech.askOpen: Is a **{space}** Action space open (not World Council)?
ui.dialog.mech.askOpenPlace: Is a **{space}** Action space open (not World Council)? Place the {bot}’s {figure} on the topmost one.
ui.dialog.mech.blinkFirst: Don’t place anything yet — the {bot} Blink-checks first, and a Blink moves an Exosuit it already has on the board instead.
ui.dialog.mech.coreNoBlink: Put an Energy Core from the supply into that Exosuit. (No Blink is possible, so it places as usual.)
ui.dialog.mech.place: Place the {bot}’s {figure} on the topmost available **{space}** Action space (or a World Council space if none are free).
ui.dialog.mine.ask: **Is there one or more Mining Action space available?**
ui.dialog.mine.blinkSub: Nothing to place yet — the Blink check comes first, and a Blink moves an Exosuit the {bot} already has on the board into that space instead.
ui.dialog.mine.find: Find the open **Mine** space granting the best 2 Resources by priority order below, based on lacking-first. Give it those **2 Resources** (pre-selected; adjust to match the space — click a cube twice for **×2**), then **discard those 2 Resource cubes from the board**.
ui.dialog.mine.place: Place the {bot}’s Exosuit in an open **Mine** space granting the best 2 Resources by priority order below, based on lacking-first. Give it those **2 Resources** (pre-selected; adjust to match the space — click a cube twice for **×2**), then **discard those 2 Resource cubes from the board**.
ui.dialog.mine.yesOpen: ✓ Yes — a Mining space is open
ui.dialog.recruit.instruct: Recruit the highest-priority **Worker** the {bot} lacks by the priority order below (missing-first); if that type isn’t available, take the next available one. Pick the recruited Worker (+1 VP) — then discard its Worker tile from the board.
ui.dialog.research.newShape: Difficulty: the {bot} takes a Breakthrough shape it doesn't already have (or has the fewest of) — a **{shape}** Breakthrough.
ui.dialog.research.rolled: The shape die rolled **{shape}** — the {bot} keeps a **{shape}** Breakthrough.
ui.dialog.timeTravel.anyPast: Remove one of the {bot}’s **Warp tiles** from the past Timeline tile where it has the most (oldest if tied).
ui.dialog.timeTravel.failCurrentEra: Failed Action: the {bot}’s only Warp tiles are on the **current Era’s Timeline tile**, which Time Travel may not take from — it takes **+{vp} VP** instead (no Exosuit placed).
ui.dialog.timeTravel.failNone: Failed Action: the {bot} has **no Warp tiles** on the Timeline, so it cannot Time Travel — it takes **+{vp} VP** instead (no Exosuit placed).
ui.dialog.timeTravel.fromEra: Remove one of the {bot}’s **Warp tiles** from **{tile}** — the past tile where it has the most (oldest if tied).
ui.dialog.wc.ask: No **{space}** space was open. Is the **World Council** space open?
ui.dialog.wc.askPlace: No **{space}** space was open. Is the **World Council** space open? Place the {bot}’s {figure} there instead.

ui.setup.app.bullets:
The Chronobot receives its 6 Exosuits and 8 Warp tiles; it does not receive any Starting Assets or Workers.
Leave all Endgame Condition cards in the box.
The Chronobot does not use a Focus marker.
Place the Chronobot’s Banner on the First Player spot; it is the First Player in the 1st Era. You receive 1 additional Water (for being the second player).
You may still choose to use either the “A” or the “B” side of your Player board.
For a more challenging game, use the variant rule described in the base game rulebook: cover the right World Council space with a Hex Unavailable tile.

ui.tileInstr.acquireGuardian: acquires a Guardian — an Exosuit onto the World Council space (becoming First Player) and the leftmost available Guardian for free, or, if that space is taken, a spent Worker instead
ui.tileInstr.adventure: performs an Adventure — an Exosuit onto the Adventure board's hex pool and a Path marker on the topmost free Power slot, then it draws 2 Adventure cards (from the 10+ deck at 9 or more Power, otherwise the 5+ deck), rolls the Adventure die, and takes the card with the highest Power requirement it meets (just +1 VP if it meets neither). Then it fulfils a Power Upgrade
ui.tileInstr.assimilate: Assimilates — roll the Research shape die: Circle, it recruits an Operator and gains 1 Flux Core; Triangle, it takes a Technology card (secondary stack); Square, whichever it has fewer of (Operator if tied). An Operator is a wildcard Worker — it fills the topmost empty space of the Worker collection (with none left in the Valley it is a Failed Action for +1 VP)

ui.tileInstr.experiment: executes a Level {level} Experiment — it takes the leftmost one carrying one of its Path markers and discards that marker, then, unless the Doomsday tracks are locked, moves its own tracker one step and takes the VP printed there. Then it prepares for Experimentation, putting a Path marker on an unmarked face-up Experiment (Level 1 before Level 2, furthest in the past to break a tie, never the one under the next Era). Either step can fail on its own, and a failed step is simply skipped
